To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the frequency of blood E‐rosettes was significantly lower in patients with distant metastases than in patients without metastases and that a low frequency of E‐ rosettes was significantly associated with a poor survival.

the blood lymphocytes of operable breast cancer patients were significantly reduced in patients with extensive tumor disease, and that a high frequency of EAC rosette‐forming (mainly B cell) lymphocytes was associated with the presence of large tumor lesions, whereas a high frequency of blood E‐rosettes was associated with a high risk of distant metastases and a poor prognosis.
the frequency of blood E‐rosettes is related to the development of metastases and the survival of breast cancer patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the possible role of the immune system in the control of breast cancer.
the relation between the extent of the primary tumor and blood lymphocyte counts and subsets in patients with breast cancer.
the relation between blood lymphocyte counts and subsets and the extent of tumor burden in breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the prognostic value and clinical significance of lymphocyte subsets and blood lymphocyte counts in breast cancer patients is still unclear and needs further investigation.

the lymphocyte counts and the frequency of E rosette‐forming T‐cells are not related to the extent of the tumor disease, but the prognosis is worse when the frequency of E ‐rosette‐ forming cells is high.

the lymphocyte count and the frequency of E rosette‐forming blood lymphocytes may be of prognostic value in breast cancer, whereas the frequency of EACA‐rosette forming lymphocytes may be a reflection of the primary tumor burden.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in breast cancer, lymphocyte counts and the proportion of E‐ and EAC‐rosetting cells in the blood may have a prognostic significance and may reflect the tumor disease.

the frequency of circulating E‐rosettes correlates to the extent of the tumor disease and to survival, and that the frequency of the EAC‐rosetting lymphocytes correlates to the extent and the prognosis of the tumor disease in patients without axilary node involvement.

in breast cancer the frequency of E rosette‐forming T cells is related to the extent of the disease and to the patient's prognosis, whereas the number of B cells is inversely related to the size of the primary tumor and is independent of the patient's prognosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a careful analysis is required in order to avoid false conclusions in this area of research.
lymphocyte subsets should be considered in the assessment of the immunological status in cancer patients.
the lymphocyte subsets may be useful for the evaluation of the prognosis in breast cancer patients.
